openingPrayer.title: Steady My Heart
openingPrayer.body: Lord, before I read what today holds, still my heart in You. The world carries heavy news and fragile hope, but You remain unshaken, near to the brokenhearted and just in all Your ways. Give me eyes to see beyond headlines, a heart that grieves rightly and hopes deeply, and hands ready to love. Guard me from fear, cynicism, and numbness. Let Your peace guard my mind, and Your truth anchor my thoughts, today and always. Amen.

articles.headline: At least 16 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams into Pakistan mosque
articles.summary: A vehicle loaded with explosives struck a mosque in Pakistan during Friday prayers, killing at least 16 people, according to a senior police official cited by BBC News. The attack occurred during a time of communal worship, and further details on the perpetrators or motive have not yet been confirmed.

articles.headline: Poland's prime minister warns of Russian 'accidental' attacks on Ukraine's allies
articles.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia could stage attacks on NATO members that appear 'accidental,' according to NPR. Tusk said such strikes are intended to test and paralyze NATO's collective defense commitments, suggesting Russia may be seeking to show that Article 5 protections exist 'only in theory.'

verse.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth gives way, though the mountains be moved into the heart of the sea.
verse.reflection: In a world where violence strikes even places of worship and nations brace for the next threat, this psalm doesn't ask us to pretend the danger isn't real—it points us to a steadier ground beneath our fear. May those grieving today find that refuge is still near, even when the earth feels unsteady.

articles.headline: The driver who slammed into an LA bus before helicopter crash is charged with murder
articles.summary: Prosecutors in Los Angeles have charged an SUV driver with murder, alleging she was under the influence of drugs when she swerved into oncoming traffic, ran a red light, and struck a city bus, according to NPR. Two bus riders were killed in the collision, which occurred before a separate helicopter crash also mentioned in the report.

articles.headline: It's illegal for armed federal officers to be at polls. Lawsuits seek to ensure that
articles.summary: According to NPR, a newly filed lawsuit argues that the Trump administration's repeated suggestions that federal officers could be present at polling sites amount to illegal voter intimidation. The suit is part of a broader legal effort seeking to affirm that armed federal officers are legally barred from polling locations.

verse.text: He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.reflection: Today's stories—one about accountability after a devastating loss of life, another about safeguarding the basic fairness of our elections—both point to a deep human longing for justice. This verse reminds us that seeking justice isn't just a civic duty; it's woven into what it means to walk faithfully with God.

articles.headline: White House withdraws nomination of Lance Schroyer to lead ICE
articles.summary: The White House has withdrawn its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to head U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to NPR. The withdrawal comes roughly three months after President Trump first nominated him for the position. No reason for the withdrawal was given in the report.

articles.headline: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
articles.summary: Two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in advertising ahead of the midterms, according to NPR, focusing primarily on traditionally safe Republican House and Senate races that have become competitive. The spending is described as a response to a challenging political environment for the GOP.

verse.text: I urge, then, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercession and thanksgiving be made for all people—for kings and all those in authority, that we may live peaceful and quiet lives in all godliness and holiness.
verse.reflection: Behind every headline about nominations, campaigns, and shifting power are real people making real decisions—and Scripture calls us to lift them up in prayer rather than only in opinion. Whatever your view of today's political maneuvering, this verse invites a posture of intercession over anxiety.

articles.headline: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
articles.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after holding the role for more than 50 years, according to NPR. His son, Howard Buffett, will succeed him as the company's new chairman.

articles.headline: Brewdog's unpaid workers to receive nothing after takeover deal
articles.summary: Administrators overseeing a takeover deal for Brewdog say unpaid workers will not recover the roughly £489,000 owed to them in wages and holiday pay, according to BBC News. The company also owed £2.4m to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

verse.text: Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act.
verse.reflection: Today's news holds both a legacy of long, careful stewardship and the pain of workers left without what they were owed. This verse reminds us that how we handle money and power matters deeply to God, especially when others depend on our faithfulness.

articles.headline: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands
articles.summary: King Charles convened a summit in Ayrshire, Scotland, bringing together leaders from AI companies including Nvidia, OpenAI, and Anthropic, according to BBC News. He reportedly warned of the 'existential danger' posed by AI technology if it fell into the wrong hands. NPR separately reported on mounting fears among experts that unchecked artificial intelligence could pose a broader threat to humanity.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by BBC News and NPR

articles.headline: Residents file lawsuit challenging noise pollution from Elon Musk's data center
articles.summary: According to NPR, residents living near Elon Musk's data center outside Memphis have filed a lawsuit over noise pollution, alleging that massive gas turbines at the facility run continuously. The suit reflects tensions between the rapid buildout of AI-related infrastructure and its impact on surrounding communities.
articles.trustNote: Reported twice by NPR; single-outlet coverage

verse.text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.
verse.reflection: As leaders and scientists voice real concern about where AI might lead us, this verse offers a steadying reminder: wisdom and discernment, not fear, are the posture God calls us to as we navigate powerful new tools shaping our world.

articles.headline: Doctors raise concerns about views and experience of members on federal task force
articles.summary: According to NPR, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has appointed new members to the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, an influential body that helps determine which preventive care services Americans receive. NPR reports that some doctors are concerned the new appointees are specialists rather than experts in preventive or general medicine, raising questions about the panel's direction.

articles.headline: New hope for breast cancer patients as life-extending drug now on NHS in England
articles.summary: BBC News reports that the drug Enhertu, which studies suggest can extend patients' lives by an average of seven months, has now been approved for prescription on the NHS in England. The outlet notes the drug has already been available to patients in Scotland for more than two years.

verse.text: For the Lord gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
verse.reflection: Today's news holds both hope and uncertainty — a new treatment easing suffering, and questions about who guides decisions affecting public health. In both, we can pray for the wisdom that only God gives, trusting that even complex systems and hard diagnoses are held within His care.

articles.headline: Mice with human brain cells offer a tool to study disease. Ethicists ask: What's next?
articles.summary: Researchers at Stanford University have genetically altered mice so they can receive and function with human brain cells, according to BBC News. NPR reports this advance could give scientists a new way to study conditions such as cerebral palsy, while ethicists are raising questions about what the development means for how these animals should be treated.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by 2 outlets (BBC News and NPR)

articles.headline: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
articles.summary: NPR reports that a bacterial infection is devastating Florida's citrus trees, threatening the state's citrus industry. Growers are hopeful that a new rootstock developed using gene-editing technology could help keep the disease in check.

verse.text: For the Lord gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
verse.reflection: As researchers push into new territory—editing genes to save orchards, blending human and animal biology to fight disease—this verse points us to the source of all true wisdom. We can be grateful for minds capable of such discovery while praying they're guided by understanding that honors both creation and human dignity.

articles.headline: Cissie Graham Lynch, granddaughter of Billy Graham, tapped for religious freedom ambassador
articles.summary: According to RNS, Cissie Graham Lynch, granddaughter of the late evangelist Billy Graham, has been nominated for the role of U.S. Ambassador-at-Large for International Religious Freedom. The report notes the position has remained vacant since the start of the second Trump administration and would require Senate confirmation.

articles.headline: Why are women leaving churches and where are they going instead? A journalist explains.
articles.summary: RNS reports on journalist Sarah Stankorb's new book, 'Damned If She Does: Why Women Quit Church and What It Means for the Future of Religion,' released this week. The book examines why women are departing from churches and what that trend may signal for the broader future of religious life.

verse.text: And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
verse.reflection: As stories today touch on who holds voice and place within faith communities — from a new religious freedom ambassador to women reconsidering their place in the pews — this verse reminds us that church was always meant to be a place of mutual encouragement, not exclusion. May today's leaders and congregations take that call seriously.

articles.headline: Tuchel recalls Alexander-Arnold and Palmer with warning
articles.summary: England manager Thomas Tuchel has recalled Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer to the national squad, according to BBC Sport. Tuchel reportedly stated that inclusion depends on players continuing to perform well for their clubs.

articles.headline: Tailgate parties, marching bands... and Ted Lasso? Wembley hosts US college game
articles.summary: Wembley Stadium will host its first American college football game this Saturday, BBC Sport reports. The event is expected to draw a crowd of around 60,000, featuring traditional college football elements like tailgate parties and marching bands.

verse.text: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.
verse.reflection: Whether it's a national team manager reminding players they must perform, or a stadium preparing to welcome thousands to a new tradition, today's sports stories carry the weight of expectation and effort. This verse offers a gentle reframe—our best effort matters not just for approval or applause, but as an offering worth giving fully.

articles.headline: British rapper Sway dies aged 44
articles.summary: BBC News reports that British rapper Sway has died at the age of 44. He was known for hits including 'Still Speedin'' and 'Level Up,' and was reportedly living in Ghana at the time of his death.

articles.headline: Oasis will not headline Glastonbury 2027, organiser Emily Eavis confirms
articles.summary: Glastonbury organiser Emily Eavis has confirmed that Oasis will not headline the festival in 2027, according to BBC News. The band will reportedly be on tour at that time next summer but will not perform at Worthy Farm.

verse.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens... a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance.
verse.reflection: Today's headlines hold both grief and the ordinary rhythms of change—a life ended too soon, and a band's plans shifting for a future season. Scripture reminds us that both sorrow and change have their place under God's care, and neither catches Him by surprise.

closingBlessing: Whatever today holds, go into it steady — you've already been reminded who's holding it. — Numbers 6:24-26
